summary: Mid-generation connection reset for streaming chat during high-burst traffic (SSE/WebSocket)
description:
Issue summary: While handling sustained high-burst traffic from customer LexiChat (dedicated pool), streaming chat connections (SSE and WebSocket) are being reset mid-generation. This typically occurs 20-90s after generation start and results in partial output (tokens missing) and the client receiving a connection reset or silent stall.

Impact: Multiple LexiChat customer sessions see mid-response disconnects or permanent stalls; affects revenue-critical chat features. Reported as repeatable during peak bursts of concurrent streaming sessions (~600 concurrent streams). Estimated ~12% of streaming sessions for this customer are impacted during bursts.

Environment: prod-us-east, dedicated cluster lexichat-ded-3, routing via streaming-proxy v2.9.1 and api-gateway v1.14. Serving runtime: gpt-redwood-XL-v1 pinned, model variant q4o.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Start sustained load test mimicking LexiChat traffic profile (burst QPS spikes to 600, average response length ~350 tokens). 2) Open streaming sessions via WebSocket and SSE clients with keepalive heartbeats disabled on client side. 3) Observe sessions for 3+ minutes; failures reproducible after ~20-90s in a subset of streams.

Observed behavior: - Client sees: ECONNRESET or abrupt socket close; for SSE the event stream terminates without a final close event. - Server logs: streaming-proxy reports repeated "write: broken pipe" and "connection reset by peer" entries; api-gateway logs show 502/523 spikes. - Metrics: streaming-proxy CPU threads spike and ephem FD count climbs just before failures; per-instance network TX stalls reported. - No consistent model-side OOMs in serving-runtime; KV cache hits stable.

Expected behavior: Streaming sessions should remain open until generation completes or a clear error with a retry/fallback policy is applied. No mid-generation silent drops.

Initial hypotheses: 1) streaming-proxy or its connection pool hits FD limits / thread starvation under burst causing RSTs. 2) A proxy-level timeout or TCP half-close race on long-lived streaming connections triggered by aggressive upstream retries. 3) Keepalive/heartbeat mismatch between client and proxy causing proxy to recycle sockets.

Logs and traces: See Grafana panels (streaming-proxy CPU, FD count): https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming?orgId=1&var-cluster=lexichat-ded-3. Sentry events: https://sentry.redwood/issue/STREAM-5342. Example proxy log snippets attached (s3 link): s3://redwood-support/logs/SUP-136478/proxy-logs-0310.txt.

Temporary workaround provided to customer: - Reduced concurrent streaming concurrency to max 250 per instance and enabled client-side keepalive heartbeats (30s) which reduced but did not eliminate failures. - Recommended moving a subset of high-length responses to polling (non-stream) endpoints as fallback until mitigation rolled out.

Next steps requested: - SRE to review FD limits and ulimit/tcp parameters on streaming-proxy layer and increase if necessary. - Engineering to repro in staging with identical connection churn and run strace on proxy during repro. - Add more granular streaming-proxy metrics (per-connection age, open FDs per worker) and correlate with failure windows. - Consider backpressure changes or graceful draining logic in streaming-proxy to avoid abrupt RSTs.
